svg.text: MPx Char: Sealed Mini Pyrolysis Capsule for Used Filters

A palm-sized steel capsule that sits on an ordinary LPG stove. The filter and its microplastics are heated without air; the vapours are burned in a catalytic cartridge, and a small carbon pellet is left.
A · On a kitchen gas stove
1 · Steel capsule: sealed, no flame touches the plastic
2 · Relief weight, like a pressure cooker
5 · Catalytic cartridge, heated by the same flame
6 · Finned tube: cools the cleaned gas
8 · Use under the chimney or at a window
Capsule about 6 cm wide × 8 cm tall;
the whole kit fits in a lunch tiffin.
B · Section: where the plastic goes
3 · Lime (CaO) pellets: trap HCl from PVC
Share of each material after heating to ~500 °C
vapour: burned to CO₂ + H₂O in the catalyst
HCl gas: held by the lime pellets
char / carbon: stays in the capsule
Plastic mostly leaves as vapour, not carbon.
The black pellet you tip out is mainly biochar
from the filter paper (≈0.1–0.2 g), plus traces
of plastic char and mineral ash. That is why the
catalyst, not the crucible, is the key part.
a small carbon pellet: not a microplastic,
goes in dry waste or into soil as biochar.
capsule sits on the pan support;
the same flame heats the catalyst
for cooking, too cool for this
Not for homes: Class 4 burn and
eye hazard; heats only a spot
Energy is tiny: heating a ~50 g steel capsule to 500 °C takes about 12 kJ,
a couple of minutes on a low flame.
E · One cycle, and the danger zone
200–450 °C: dioxins can form in cooling gas [2]
catalyst (heats first, being nearer the flame)
Vapours reach the catalyst while it is already hot, and only cool after they are oxidised. Open only when the dial is blue.
F · Safety for an Indian home
Sealed: no open flame ever touches plastic.
Relief weight works like a pressure cooker's.
Cool-touch handle; fits any pan support.
Lime pellets hold HCl if PVC is present.
Run under the chimney or by an open window.
Never open hot; keep children away.
Industrial rules require gases at 850 °C or more
needs an emissions test (CO, VOCs, dioxins).
Open burning of plastic is not allowed
in India [4]. A sealed, tested unit is different,
but claims need testing and approval first.
Amounts are milligrams: low risk, not zero.

[1] EU Industrial Emissions Directive 2010/75/EU, Art. 50: gas held at ≥850 °C for 2 s (≥1,100 °C if over 1% halogenated organics). [2] US EPA (2003). Dioxin reassessment, Part I Vol. 1 Ch. 2: formation in combustion.

[3] Gebre, S.H. et al. (2021). Recent trends in the pyrolysis of non-degradable waste plastics. ChemistryOpen 10, 1202–1226. [4] Plastic Waste Management Rules, 2016 (India), Rules 6(2)(g) and 7(c): ensure open burning of plastic waste does not take place.
